paras: The lynching of Morgan Williams was the killing of a Black man by a group of Black men in Canton, Mississippi, in late July 1888. According to the only report found, Williams, a stranger in the town, had killed a man named Morgan Jones while defending himself against Jones's attacks. The report named the lynchers only as "negroes" and treated the episode as one item among the week's state news.

The Brookhaven Leader reported that Williams, described as "a negro," was "lynched by negroes in Canton last week, for defending himself against the attacks of Morgan Jones whom he killed." The item added that "Williams was a stranger in town." It gave no names of the lynchers, no number, no account of how Williams was killed, and no race for Jones.
No report of an inquest, arrests or prosecution appears in the coverage.

The story survives in a single sentence in the Brookhaven Leader of August 2, 1888, in "The State," a column of "news items gathered and condensed from all quarters" of Mississippi. There it ran without a headline or comment, between a note urging a Blue and Grey reunion at Vicksburg and news of a Magnolia editor's medical treatment. The same column carried other violence of the week in equally brief form, including a report that "five or six negroes murdered two white men near Yazoo City" and the hanging of Eli Bryan in Winston County.

The item presented Williams's self-defense as fact, stating it as the reason he was lynched without comment on the killing of Jones or on the lynchers. No other report of the lynching, local or by wire, appears in the coverage.

reader.title: Lynching of Morgan Williams
bases: The only report says Williams 'was lynched by negroes' in Canton, the act of a group outside any legal process (A1).

A1 says Williams was 'lynched' by 'negroes' (plural, number not given) for killing Morgan Jones, which implies an extralegal killing in retaliation for a homicide; the size of the group and the manner of death are not reported, so the three-or-more element rests on the word 'lynched' alone.
One condensed news item in the Brookhaven Leader (A1) is the only report found; no local Canton paper, wire story or follow-up appears in the coverage.
